source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

morphology_documented.stems: Young stems usually densely pubescent, occasionally nearly glabrous
morphology_documented.leaves: Opposite and short-petioled; oblong-ovate or oblong-lanceolate, juvenile leaves often pinnatifid; uppermost leaves separate
morphology_documented.flowers: Fragrant corollas 25–40 mm long, creamy-white or purple-tinged, becoming yellow then brownish; tube externally pubescent; at least two lobes of upper lip united more than halfway; flowers primarily axillary in pairs (genus key)
morphology_documented.habitat: Cultivated, escaped in disturbed areas, woods and thickets; native to Asia
